faqs.answer: A root canal removes infected or inflamed tissue from inside a tooth to relieve pain and save the natural tooth. Most patients feel little to no discomfort thanks to local anesthesia, and it typically takes one to two visits.
A routine dental cleaning removes plaque and tartar buildup and usually takes about 30 to 45 minutes. It is recommended every six months to maintain healthy gums and teeth.
Braces and clear aligners gradually straighten teeth over time. Treatment length varies by case, generally between 12 and 24 months, and starts with an orthodontic consultation.
Teeth whitening lightens tooth discoloration using safe, dentist-supervised bleaching agents. In-clinic treatments typically show visible results in a single session.
A tooth extraction removes a damaged, decayed, or impacted tooth under local anesthesia. Most extractions are quick, and the dentist will provide simple aftercare instructions for a smooth recovery.
A dental implant replaces a missing tooth root with a titanium post topped with a custom crown, offering a long-lasting, natural-looking, and stable replacement tooth.
A general dental checkup includes an oral examination, a review of your dental history, and a discussion of any concerns, helping catch issues early before they become bigger problems.
